name: Ahead-of-the-Storm-DATAPIPELINE
what_it_holds: UNICEF Data & Predictive Analytics pipeline that ingests and processes tropical-storm/hurricane 'envelope' geospatial data for impact analysis (originally built for child-population exposure, but the storm-track/impact-footprint ingestion is domain-agnostic). 2 stars.
why_useful: A ready-made pipeline pattern for turning storm tracks into geographic exposure footprints, which could be repointed at STR-market exposure (which Inside Airbnb markets/zip codes sit inside a given storm's cone) for the RNPL/cancellation thesis (gap #11, #3).
time_coverage: depends on storm data source ingested (likely NOAA/IBTrACS-based)
size_hint: pipeline code, not a fixed dataset

name: Hurdat2Converter
what_it_holds: Script converting NOAA's raw HURDAT2 fixed-format text file into a clean, analysis-ready CSV/table (storm id, date, position, wind, pressure).
why_useful: Alternative lightweight tool to the R package above for the same hurricane best-track series, useful if the team's pipeline is Python-only.

name: backburner
what_it_holds: R utilities for collecting open US wildfire data plus matched climate features (weather station data joined to fire events).
why_useful: Alternative/older tooling for assembling a US wildfire event panel with weather covariates, useful if the team wants wildfire dates outside California too (e.g., Pacific Northwest markets not yet in the Inside Airbnb panel).
